chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) ruled in a case of two men who claimed a mule. One of them established two witnesses against his companion, and the other established five. So he ruled for the one with the five witnesses, five portions, and for the one with the two witnesses, two portions.
ai.seo_question: How did Imam Ali rule on a dispute where two parties presented different numbers of witnesses?
ai.summary: This hadith from Al-Kafi illustrates the principle of proportional justice in Shia jurisprudence, where the evidentiary weight of witnesses is not merely binary but quantitative. Imam Ali (peace be upon him) awarded five shares to the claimant with five witnesses and two shares to the one with two, demonstrating a flexible approach to testimony that values the quantity of credible witnesses. This ruling highlights the practical application of judicial discretion (ijtihad) in early Islamic courts to ensure equitable outcomes based on the strength of evidence.
